resources.string: Use your fingerprint or phone PIN

Everything you add stays on this phone and is always encrypted. Mandat has no internet access. It opens with your fingerprint or the phone PIN.\n\nImportant: if you remove the phone\'s screen lock, the data can no longer be opened. Keep an encrypted backup (Options → Backup).
Set a screen lock (PIN or password) on the phone first. Mandat uses it to protect your data.

The encryption key is no longer available (for example, the screen lock was removed or the app data was partly lost). Mandat will not delete anything by itself. Your data can be restored from an encrypted backup.
Inbox is empty. Tap + to note anything that is on your mind.
One file with all your data, encrypted with your password. Save it wherever you like: a USB stick, a computer, your own cloud. Use it to restore data or move to a new phone or tablet.
Working… this takes a few seconds.
At least 16 characters. A few random words work best. Keep the password separately from the file: without it nobody can open the backup, not even you.
At least 16 characters, and not too simple.

Mandat opens with your fingerprint or the phone PIN, locks when you leave it, blocks screenshots by default and has no internet access. You can change the phone PIN or password, but never turn the screen lock off completely: Android then destroys the key, and the data on this phone can no longer be opened, even if the lock is turned on again. Make a fresh backup before changing the screen lock.
Version %1$s. Not for classified information. Open source (GPL-3.0). Written with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic), directed and tested by the author.
Start over and restore from a backup
The data on this phone cannot be opened any more. Starting over deletes it from this phone for good. Then restore your data from a backup: Options → Backup → Restore from a backup.

Unlock with the phone\'s PIN or password only, without a fingerprint: a finger can be forced onto the sensor, a PIN has to be said. Takes effect at the next unlock.
Hidden from every screen while trip mode is on.
Hides sensitive matters from the screens, for example before crossing a border.

What it does: matters marked as sensitive, and everything linked to them (delegations, promises, deadlines, events, media items, key messages, alliances, money, aid records, links with people), disappear from every screen, list, chart and search. Events from the phone calendar are not shown either. The data stays encrypted on the phone; nothing is deleted.

What stays visible: people, communities, diary entries, the Inbox and topic names (only their links to hidden matters disappear), the switch itself and the "Sensitive" mark.

What it does not do: it does not protect against someone who makes you unlock Mandat and knows where to turn it off (one switch in Options). Backups, including automatic ones on the phone, contain everything. Copies of events added to the phone calendar stay there. Restoring an older backup removes the marks.

For crossing a border it is safer to also turn on "PIN only", make a backup with a password, move automatic backups off the phone and remove the sensitive matters for the trip. GrapheneOS also has a duress PIN that wipes the phone.

Answers questions from your records, gives a morning overview and drafts the evening entry, splits a letter, notes or the Inbox into matters, delegations and deadlines, suggests the next step, writes a brief, a summary of the week, a draft rebuttal and key messages, helps with texts and checks the language. Everything is in the AI Center (the ✦ mark at the top). Works entirely on the phone, without internet; it only suggests — what you confirm is saved. The model takes about 2.6 GB.
